units: B. Bath. IV, 7 המוכר … מכר את הס׳ if one sells a township, he sells with it the sanṭer (a slave, v. אִיקוֹנוֹמוֹס); expl.
ib. באגי the fields around the town]; Tosef. ib. III, 5.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 98b:8">Snh. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>פגע בו ס׳</he> a bailiff meets him (trying to contest his title to the field).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 5:5:9">Y. B. Mets. V, 10ᶜ</cite> <he>ישראל שמינה … או ס׳</he> an Israelite who appointed a gentile his manager or guardsman.

<cite ref="Gittin 80b:1">Gitt. 80ᵇ</cite> <he>אפי׳ … לשם ס׳ שבעיר</he> even if he dates a letter of divorce from the rule of a bailiff of the town. Tanḥ. B’rakhah 6 <he>כס׳ הזה וכ׳</he> like the guardsman that speaks before the king; a. e.

senses.gloss: the guarded land outside of a township. B. Bath. l. c., v. supra.
(cmp. meanings of לֶחִי, and phrases like שמר פתחי פיך, Mic. VII, 5) [fence,] jaw, jawbone, chin.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 24b:1">Ber. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>וכשהוא … מניח ידו על סַנְטֵרוֹ</he> (Ms. M. <he>סַנְטֵירוֹ</he>) and when he yawned, he put his hand on his chin (to cover his mouth).
Treat. Der. Er. ch. XI סַנְטֵרוֹ לצדדין וקובעו וכ׳ he who walks with his sanṭer hanging sideways and his cap turned back …, belongs to the haughty.
